_doc: The application evaluator runs each case as a baseline/no-skill arm and a with-skill arm, then grades behavior against expected_flags, expected_fix_hints, absent_signals, and the per-case criteria checklist.
subject: Use when designing or reviewing HTTP API surfaces: consumer tasks, audience class, protocol/paradigm fit,…

cases.scenario: A user asks: "design the API for listing orders with filters, pagination, and stable errors"
cases.context: The agent has access to the api-design skill and must decide whether to use it, apply its procedure, and stay inside its boundaries.
cases.question: What should the agent do, and why is api-design the right skill to apply?
expected_flags: Recognizes api-design as applicable to this request
Uses the skill-specific purpose or mental model instead of generic advice
Names the relevant boundary against event-contract-design, entity-relationship-modeling, debugging
Turns the request into concrete steps, checks, or decisions from the skill
expected_fix_hints: Apply the api-design workflow to the concrete scenario
State the next action and the evidence or verification needed
Call out any adjacent skill that should own a different part of the request
absent_signals: Does not answer with generic advice that could ignore api-design
Does not route to event-contract-design, entity-relationship-modeling, debugging when the api-design scope is the owner
Does not invent certification, freshness, or runtime success claims without evidence
